We estimated the treatment effect with a robust covariance estimator clustered by site. The model included baseline age, enrollment month, and the prespecified severity index. Missing outcomes were not imputed; the primary estimate therefore describes participants observed at day 30.

The interval widened after clustering, from 1.8 to 3.1 percentage points, while the point estimate changed by less than 0.2 points. This result does not establish equivalence. It shows that the study was too small to distinguish a modest effect from no effect under the registered analysis.

Code, exclusions, and anonymized aggregates are included in the replication archive.
